After thirty-seven years in the field, emergency, intensive care, research, plants, cycles, one thing keeps coming back: we still try to treat the human being in pieces, when we're really one whole unit. This is the vision I carry today: uniting clinical rigor with ancestral wisdom, putting the body back at the center as a model, not a machine to repair, giving every woman the keys to understand, decide, and organize her life around what her body is showing her. I'm currently nominated in the pioneer category at the Quebec Integrative Health Congress. For me, this vote isn't about a title. It's a way of saying this approach, refusing silos, respecting the body's authority, uniting different kinds of knowledge, deserves more room in today's landscape. There's still a bit of time to vote. If this way of seeing health resonates with you, I invite you to add your voice to mine.
